gloss: To raise one's eyebrows and exhale, meaning to feel proud and relieved.
teaser: Today, we explore a phrase that embodies pride and relief.
script: Welcome to Chengyu Bites — your quick summary on Chinese 成语. Today, we explore a phrase that embodies pride and relief. [break 1s] The phrase is: 扬眉吐气, yángméi tǔqì. [break 1s] 扬 (yáng) - to raise [break 0.5s] 眉 (méi) - eyebrows [break 0.5s] 吐 (tǔ) - to exhale [break 0.5s] 气 (qì) - breath [break 1s] So, 扬眉吐气 literally means 'to raise eyebrows and exhale,' but figuratively it signifies feeling proud and relieved. [break 1s] Here’s the story behind it: [break 1.5s] This idiom originates from the feeling of triumph after overcoming challenges, where one can finally lift their eyebrows and breathe out a sigh of relief. It often describes moments when someone feels vindicated or successful after a struggle. The image of raising eyebrows symbolizes confidence and satisfaction. [break 1.5s] Example 1: 他通过了考试，终于扬眉吐气。 [break 1s] He passed the exam and finally feels proud and relieved. [break 1s] Example 2: 她在比赛中获胜，扬眉吐气。 [break 1s] She won the competition and felt proud and relieved. [break 1s] Example 3: 经过多年的努力，他终于扬眉吐气。 [break 1s] After years of hard work, he finally feels proud and relieved. [break 1s] So that’s 扬眉吐气, which means to feel proud and relieved. Thank you for listening to Chengyu Bites! See you next time for another idiom. [break 1s]
